purpose: Development regression used during prompt tuning; not independent clinical validation
prompt:
A 59-year-old male presents to the emergency department with chest pain.

Patient ID: MF-CARD-001
Age: 59 years
Sex: Male
Weight: 83 kg

Chief complaint: Central chest pressure for 90 minutes, radiating to the left arm and jaw. Pain severity 7/10. Associated sweating, nausea and mild breathlessness. Pain started while walking and continued despite resting.

Medical history: Type 2 diabetes for 11 years, hypertension for 8 years, dyslipidemia. Smokes 10 cigarettes daily. Father suffered myocardial infarction at age 54. No previous diagnosed coronary artery disease.

Medications: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily, losartan 50 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg nightly (irregular adherence). Took sildenafil 50 mg approximately 8 hours ago.

Allergies: No known drug allergies. No history of active bleeding or peptic ulcer bleeding. Not taking anticoagulants.

Vital signs: BP 146/88 mmHg, HR 106 bpm, RR 21/min, SpO2 97% on room air, Temp 36.8 C.

Physical exam: Alert, anxious and sweating. Heart sounds normal, regular tachycardia. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema. No chest wall tenderness. Peripheral pulses symmetrical.

ECG: Sinus tachycardia, approximately 1 mm horizontal ST depression in V4-V6, no ST elevation.

Labs: hs-troponin I 11 ng/L (lab upper reference limit 19 ng/L), creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, eGFR 55 mL/min/1.73 m2, glucose 218 mg/dL, hemoglobin 13.9 g/dL, platelets 242000/uL, potassium 4.4 mmol/L.

The first troponin sample was obtained about 90 minutes after symptom onset. The patient continues to experience chest discomfort.
